question: In the RSC Advances study of biochar loading in dual-phase MIL-100(Al)/MIL-110(Al) hybrids for CO2 adsorption, which adsorbent in the paper's comparison table of MOF/biochar CO2 adsorbents has the highest CO2 uptake, and with which isotherm model?
rendered: According to the paper's comparison table of MOF/biochar CO2 adsorbents (Table 6), BC-10 has the highest CO2 uptake of 1.77 mmol g−1 at 298 K and 1 bar. This is consistent with the results in the paper, which states that BC-10 showed the highest cumulative weak-to-strong CO2-interaction contribution below 400 °C. The CO2 adsorption performance of BC-10 is governed by a biochar-loading-dependent structure–property relationship, and the Freundlich model fitting is evidence of the adsorption on heterogeneous energetic surfaces due to the synergistic integration of the aluminium-based framework and the activated biochar.
